title: The component-site projection for an affine scheme
statement:
Let $T$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme], and put $P=\pi_0(|T|)$, the quotient by connected components with its quotient topology [lem-pe-spectral-components-profinite]. Use the universes of [def-weil-size-convention] and the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $P_{\mathrm{proet}}$ be the site of profinite spaces over $P$ with finite jointly surjective covering families. For a profinite map $E\to P$, there is an affine ind-etale $T$-scheme $T_E$, whose underlying locally ringed space is $|T|\times_P E$ with the inverse-image structure sheaf from $T$. Its component space is canonically $E$. The functor $E\mapsto T_E$ preserves finite limits and coverings and defines a geometric morphism [def-trf-geometric-morphism]
$$\pi_T:\operatorname{Sh}(T_{\mathrm{proet}})\longrightarrow\operatorname{Sh}(P_{\mathrm{proet}}).$$
For every sheaf of sets $F$ on $P_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and every quasi-compact quasi-separated object $W\to T$ of $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ satisfying the following split-cover condition, there is a canonical identification. The condition is: for every finite pro-etale covering family $\{W_i\to W\}$ with all $W_i$ quasi-compact quasi-separated, the canonical map $p:\coprod_i W_i\to W$ has a section $\sigma:W\to\coprod_iW_i$ over $T$, with $p\sigma=\operatorname{id}_W$. The identification is
$$(\pi_T^{-1}F)(W)=F(\pi_0(|W|)\to P),$$
natural in $F$ and in maps between objects $W$ satisfying this condition. The same formula applies to sheaves of abelian groups and rings, preserving their operations.

proof.text: Set A = Γ(T, ⊤). For E → π₀(T), transport the base map through T.isoSpec and take the actual graph-restriction algebra B = WContractification.PullbackProfinite A E i. Define T_E = Spec B with its structure map followed by T.isoSpec.inv. The existing fiberHomeo, with swapped factors and the affine-scheme isomorphism, gives |T_E| = |T| ×_{π₀(T)} E and identifies both projections. PullbackProfinite.indZariski implies ind-etaleness and bijectivity of all local-ring maps. Transport these through Spec and the affine isomorphism to obtain the asserted stalk isomorphisms and IndEtaleAcrossUniverses statement.

proof.text: The projection |T_E| → E is surjective: lift E.hom e through the surjective component quotient. Each fibre is homeomorphic to a connected component of |T|, hence connected. A connected component maps constantly to the totally disconnected E. Consequently the induced map π₀(T_E) → E is bijective, and compactness and Hausdorffness make it a homeomorphism. This uses the actual quotient topology, including empty spaces.

For a ring map A → B inducing isomorphisms on local rings, the existing inverse ringHomOfHomOver constructs an A-algebra map B → C from any continuous Spec C → Spec B over Spec A. Repeat the source injectivity proof without its unused hypothesis that A → C also identifies local rings. This proves the affine mapping property for arbitrary affine W. Cover an arbitrary scheme W by affine opens, use uniqueness on their overlaps, and glue. A map E → E′ therefore gives a unique T-map T_E → T_E′; uniqueness proves the functor laws and the projection formula. The same mapping property gives a natural isomorphism between its covariant Hom functors and Hom in the topological slice. The topological-slice functor preserves finite limits, and coyoneda jointly reflects limits, proving finite-limit preservation.

For a finite jointly surjective family E_i → E, lift each point of |T_E| through the fibre homeomorphisms. Each induced morphism T_Ei → T_E is weakly etale by cancellation against its weakly etale target structure map. It is quasi-compact because it is a map of affine schemes. The finite family is therefore a pro-etale covering. CoverPreserving follows from the effective-epimorphic-family description of the coherent slice topology. Finite-limit preservation gives representable flatness; cover preservation and flatness give continuity.

For qcqs W, the scheme mapping property factors uniquely through π₀(W), giving the natural equivalence Hom_T(W,T_E) = Hom_P(π₀(W),E). The associated costructured-arrow category has a terminal object. Apply its pointwise left Kan colimit to obtain P(F)(W) ≅ F(π₀(W)) and compute its normalization against every map W → T_E. This equivalence is natural in E, W, and F.

source.place: Functor.LeftExtension.IsPointwiseLeftKanExtension; isIso_ι_app_of_isTerminal; the private componentFactorEquiv, kanTerminal and kanEvaluation proofs

proof.text: The coherent topology of Profinite/P contains its extensive topology: forgetting a finite coproduct cofan gives an effective epimorphic family in Profinite. Hence a sheaf on Profinite/P preserves finite products. Use the qcqs finite-coproduct evaluation theorem to construct the coproduct of a finite qcqs family in the pro-etale site. Its component object is the coproduct in Profinite/P by the quotient universal property. Transport the preceding Kan evaluation isomorphisms along these two coproducts. This proves that P(F) takes finite qcqs disjoint unions to products, also for the empty family.

A covering sieve on a qcqs W contains a finite affine covering family, by the quasi-compact-cover refinement theorem. Reindex it by Fin n, apply the stated split-cover condition, and transport the scheme section to a section in the pro-etale site. For the sheafification unit η:P(F) → P(F)#, the equalizer sieve of two sections with equal image is covering. On this split finite refinement their restrictions agree; injectivity of the finite-product restriction makes their pullbacks along the coproduct map agree. Pull back by the section to prove injectivity of η_W. The image sieve of any sheafified section is also covering. Lift on each summand, combine by the finite-product bijection, compare the two sheaf sections on the coproduct, and pull back by the section. This proves surjectivity. For a concrete coefficient category the forgetful functor preserves these products and reflects isomorphisms, so η_W is an isomorphism in that category.

source.place: Scheme.QuasiCompactCover.exists_hom; Presheaf.equalizerSieve_mem and imageSieve_mem; Stacks Tags 00WB and 00WK

proof.text: Take the canonical inverse image obtained by left Kan extension followed by sheafification, with direct image actual restriction. Representable flatness makes its comma categories filtered. The general-universe flat Kan-extension theorem applies with colimit size (u,u+1); shrink AB5 for Type(u+1), and transfer it through the finite-limit-preserving, filtered-colimit-preserving forgetful functor. This makes inverse image left exact. Compose η_W inverse with the Kan evaluation to get the required evaluation isomorphism. Compute the canonical adjunction unit as the Kan unit followed by η, proving the required normalization. Use the pointwise Kan universal property, factorization naturality, and η naturality to prove the joint naturality in F and W. Apply this single argument directly in Type(u+1), AddCommGrpCat and CommRingCat; its isomorphisms preserve operations by construction.
